answer: No weight counts until one walnut per identity has sat unopened to its horizon, its 400 locked units and certified kernel mass sealed under the identity's mark. The walnut rests on a velvet pad; assayers record the imprint it compresses at sealing and re-measure that imprint at the horizon, and an imprint too shallow for the certified mass voids the weight. Opening before that horizon shatters the kernel. One honest agent locks 400 once and recovers it intact; a farm fielding 1,000 identities locks 400,000 on identical terms, and one walnut's imprint certifies no kernel but its own.
